chunks: And said: "We have come to believe in the Lord of all the worlds,
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'We have believed in the Lord of the worlds' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this declaration is often linked to the steadfastness of the Imams and the faithful during their trials, emphasizing that true belief requires acknowledging Allah as the Lord of all cosmic realms, not just a tribal deity. It underscores the universality of Tawhid, contrasting the monotheistic conviction of the believers with the polytheistic arrogance of Pharaoh's court. This verse serves as a foundational text for understanding the spiritual authority and resilience of the Ahl al-Bayt in their confrontation with earthly powers.
